extracted.intended_audience: researchers and analysts conducting content analysis of health journalism; health journalists and media scholars interested in health-news quality metrics
extracted.subtask_description: Variables and indicators for evaluating the quality of health-related news coverage, intended for content analysis of newspaper/online health articles. Includes multiple dimensions (diversity, completeness, relevance, understandability, objectiveness) and specific criteria derived from prior health-news quality frameworks (e.g., Schwitzer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequately discussion of costs associated with the treatment/approach/product described in the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the article mentions financial costs or resource implications; consider whether costs are presented in concrete terms vs. ignored. (Referenced as one of Schwitzer's common criteria for judging health coverage.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantification of benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantification of benefits — reporting benefits in numeric, absolute or relative terms rather than vague assertions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for numeric estimates, effect sizes, absolute vs relative risk, number-needed-to-treat, and clear statements of magnitude; absence or vague language is a common quality problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation and quantification of potential harms
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequate explanation and quantification of possible harms, side effects or risks associated with the treatment/idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether harms are described and quantified with comparable clarity to benefits; check for omission or minimization of risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison with existing alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison of the new idea, treatment, test or product with existing alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the article situates the new intervention relative to established options, including pros/cons and relative effectiveness; absence of comparison can overstate novelty or benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of sources and conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Independence of sources and discussion of potential conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether sources' affiliations, funding sources, and potential conflicts are disclosed and whether independent experts are consulted rather than relying solely on vested parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of disease mongering
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoidance of disease mongering — not exaggerating prevalence/severity to promote interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for sensationalist framing that widens the definition of disease, inflates risk, or promotes overdiagnosis; consider whether the article dramatizes conditions to create demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of methodology/quality of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Review of the study methodology or the overall quality of the evidence supporting claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess reporting on study design, sample size, controls, limitations, potential biases, reproducibility and overall strength of evidence; reliable coverage discusses these elements rather than only headlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion of novelty and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of the true novelty and availability of the idea, approach or product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the article clarifies whether findings are preliminary or definitive, whether the intervention is available now or years away, and whether results are incremental vs. paradigm-changing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information beyond the news release
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of information that goes beyond the original news release (adds independent reporting or context).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the piece adds independent verification, expert comment, methodological context, or other original reporting versus merely restating a press release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy via comparison with original research
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy of media coverage assessed by comparison to the original research paper or primary source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare media claims to the original study's findings, methods, numerics and stated limitations; note omissions, distortions or overgeneralizations when media diverges from primary sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: External/expert continuous evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality judged continuously by journalists, medical experts, or independent organizations (e.g., HealthNewsReview).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use expert panels, independent review organizations, or ongoing professional critique as part of assessing quality; these bodies use structured criteria (like Schwitzer's) to rate stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity (dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Diversity of coverage including quantitative diversity, source diversity, opinion diversity and article length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicators: length of the article; number and variety of sources cited; inclusion of contrary opinions; presence of multiple perspectives. Inter-rater reliability reported (rH = 0.78).

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness (dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalistic and scientific completeness of information, including coverage of prevention, symptoms, remedies, methods, sample and results, and discussion of risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicators: For diseases — info about prevention, symptoms, remedies; For research studies — method, sample, results; For treatments — addressing risks and side effects. Intended to capture whether essential factual elements are present. (rH = 0.86)

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance (dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevance of the article measured by source credibility, usefulness (take-home messages and references), and newsworthiness (topicality and news factors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicators: credibility of sources cited (reputation), presence of clear take-home messages and pointers to further information, and news factors such as timeliness. (rH = 0.85)

rubrics_metrics.name: Understandability (dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understandability measured by simplicity of language, structure, conciseness and use of storytelling vs dry presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicators: simplicity vs complexity of language; well-structured vs poorly structured presentation; concise vs circuitous wording; use of storytelling that aids comprehension. (rH = 0.86)

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectiveness (dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectivity measured via emotionalization, emotional language, and dramatization of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicators: presence of emotional wording, sensationalist framing or dramatization that undermines neutral reporting. (rH = 0.95)
